=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:629-714 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `newly_fixed` is incremented for resolver-fixed fingerprints but never surfaced in the PASSED summary.
  WHY: reviewers said the final status only reports `pre_existing_drift_count`, so resolver-fixed counts stay hidden from the primary summary.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:357-359 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: removing `_branch_suffix()` drops branch attribution from compare-mode PASSED output.
  WHY: reviewers reported that downstream consumers and PR1569-style expectations rely on branch context being present on PASSED lines.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:434-444 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_violation_message` re-resolves out-of-tree paths and can emit duplicate warning lines for repeated failures.
  WHY: reviewers said repeated resolver runs can bloat logs and confuse duplicate-alert tooling.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:608-815 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `list_violated_files()` and `verify()` treat unparseable regexes as violations instead of skipping them, changing default-mode backward compatibility and producing false positives.
  WHY: reviewers said malformed regexes now surface as violated paths even though the original code skipped them.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:560-566 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `_baseline_lookup()` falls back to `_fp_key(fp)`, but that symbol is reportedly undefined in the refactored path and can raise `NameError`.
  WHY: reviewers said malformed or hand-edited baselines without `fp_key` would crash the verifier instead of falling back cleanly.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:702-714 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `newly_fixed` counter is incremented at line 666 when fingerprints are fixed by the resolver, but this value is never surfaced in the final summary output.
  WHY: Operators and drift-audit tooling cannot quickly determine how many fingerprints were resolved by the resolver - they must parse individual `PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1 fixed_by_resolver` markers to count them.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:702-714 and verify() 771-775 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The final PASSED status lines do not include branch context, even though earlier ratio output includes `branch=...`.
  WHY: Downstream parsers or operators that grep for branch attribution in PASSED output will not find it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:680-690 | severity=low
  PROBLEM: The `newly_fixed` counter is incremented in compare mode when a baseline-unsatisfied pattern becomes satisfied, but it is never surfaced in the final summary output.
  WHY: Operators and downstream audit tooling expect to see counts of newly fixed items in the summary, but only drift count appears there.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:110-130, 610-620 | severity=low
  PROBLEM: `_violation_message` re-resolves invalid out-of-tree paths via `_resolve_repo_path` for every call, which can emit duplicate `::warning::` lines to stderr on repeated failures.
  WHY: Repeated resolver runs on an out-of-tree fingerprint path may produce duplicate warnings and confuse triage tooling.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:357-359 | severity=medium
  PROBLEM: Removal of `_branch_suffix()` eliminates branch attribution from the output contract on PASSED lines.
  WHY: Downstream parsers and the orchestrator judge expect the branch context on PASSED output; its removal breaks the exact output contract.
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
(No findings reported.)
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:643-648, 810-815 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `if not satisfied` in both `list_violated_files()` and `verify()` treats unparseable regexes as violations instead of skipping them.
  WHY: A malformed regex can now surface as a false-positive violation in both paths and can block `[ai-merge-resolve]` commits that the original code would have skipped.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:593-594 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_baseline_lookup()` falls back to `_fp_key(fp)`, but `_fp_key` is not defined in the current codebase after the refactor.
  WHY: A hand-edited or corrupted baseline that omits `fp_key` would hit a `NameError` and crash the verifier.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:640-670 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `newly_fixed` is incremented on baseline-unsatisfied → current-satisfied transitions but is never read or emitted in any summary line.
  WHY: Fixed cases become invisible in the primary status output, reducing observability for resolver effectiveness.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:690-700 and 780 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: compare-mode PASSED output no longer matches the branch-suffixed PASS shape expected by prior test fixtures and downstream consumers.
  WHY: The final compare-mode status string does not include the branch context that earlier output lines expose.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:200-220, 620-630 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_violation_message` calls `_resolve_repo_path` a second time for out-of-tree must_contain/content_unavailable paths, so duplicate `::warning::` lines can be emitted.
  WHY: Repeated verification runs can bloat logs and obscure genuine errors.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
